verdict.rationale: Svelte has no built-in natural-language interface. Its official AI tooling (an MCP server installable via `claude mcp add`, the svelte-autofixer tool and documented subagents) lets an external AI agent take natural-language requests and produce or check Svelte code. Natural-language operation therefore works only through a third-party agent client, with Svelte supplying docs and static analysis rather than interpreting commands itself. Missing for 10: a first-party natural-language command interface, documented end-to-end natural-language workflows (e.g. scaffolding or `sv add` driven by prompts), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
